html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. NAT: network address translation; VPC: Virtual Private Cloud; VPN: virtual private network; CDN: content delivery network; AZ: Availability Zone; TTL: time to live; ALB: Application Load Balancer; NLB: Network Load Balancer; CNAME: canonical name; WAF: Web Application Firewall; SQS: Simple Queue Service; EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud

  • Find where data transfer charges come from
  • Choose NAT gateway layouts and VPC endpoints that cut cost
  • Compare Direct Connect, VPN and the internet, and peering, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink
  • Use CDNs, edge caching, routing and throttling to reduce transfer
  • Review existing workloads for network savings

2Data transfer, NAT, endpoints and connectivity

Running case

Lantern and Loom Trims the Network Bill

  • Three NAT gateways run in a test VPC
  • Private servers pull terabytes from S3 through a NAT gateway
  • Overseas shoppers download images straight from the Region
  • A steady, large data feed goes to the head office over the internet
  • The network bill keeps rising: find the waste

Where Network Cost Comes From

Traffic Typical cost
Into AWS from the internet Free
Out to the internet Charged per GB
Between Regions Charged per GB
Between AZs in a Region Charged per GB, both directions
Same AZ, private IP Free
Through a NAT gateway Hourly plus per GB processed
Public IPv4 addresses Hourly charge
  • Prefer private IP paths and same-AZ traffic where the design allows
  • Exact rates change: learn the order, not the numbers
Exam tip

Data in is free; data out, across Regions and across AZs costs money.

NAT Gateway Cost [Verify live]

Layout Cost and resilience
NAT instance You pay for an instance and manage it; cheap at tiny scale, limited bandwidth, a single point of failure
One shared NAT gateway Lowest cost; cross-AZ traffic; one AZ is the failure point
One NAT gateway per AZ Higher cost; resilient; no cross-AZ NAT traffic
Regional NAT gateway One ID that expands across AZs; simpler design
  • A NAT gateway bills hourly plus per GB processed
  • As of 5 November 2026, check the regional NAT gateway pricing and Region availability
  • Non-production: one gateway is often enough
Exam tip

Production needs a NAT gateway per AZ for resilience; test and development can share one.

Avoiding NAT Cost with VPC Endpoints

  • Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB: no additional charge
  • Traffic uses a route table entry to the service prefix list
  • Interface endpoints (PrivateLink): hourly per AZ plus per GB, for most other services
  • A gateway endpoint only works for the same Region
  • Sending S3 traffic through NAT adds a per-GB charge for nothing

Exam tip

Private servers reading S3 or DynamoDB through NAT: add a gateway endpoint.

Direct Connect, VPN and the Internet

Option Cost shape Best for
Internet Data out per GB; no port Light, occasional transfer
Site-to-Site VPN Hourly per connection plus data out Quick, low-cost encrypted link
Direct Connect Port hours plus lower data-out rate Steady, high-volume, consistent latency
  • Each VPN tunnel carries up to about 1.25 Gbps; use several tunnels or Transit Gateway for more
  • Direct Connect port speed should match the real need
  • Data into AWS over any option is free
Exam tip

Large, steady transfer: Direct Connect. Quick or small: VPN. Occasional: internet.

Connecting VPCs: Peering, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink

Option Cost shape Choose it when
VPC peering No hourly fee; data across AZs or Regions charged Few VPCs, point to point
Transit Gateway Hourly per attachment plus per GB processed Many VPCs and sites; simpler routing
PrivateLink Hourly per endpoint plus per GB One service shared privately
  • Peering is not transitive: a mesh grows quickly
  • Compare the total: attachments, processing and the engineering time
Exam tip

Two or three VPCs: peering is cheapest. Many VPCs and on-premises sites: Transit Gateway.

Routing to Minimize Transfer Cost

Technique Saves
Keep chatty tiers in the same AZ Avoids cross-AZ charges (weigh against availability)
Use private IP addresses between instances Avoids public data transfer
Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB Avoids NAT processing
Same-Region buckets and compute Avoids cross-Region transfer
CloudFront in front of origins Cheaper egress and fewer origin reads
Compress and cache Fewer bytes to move
  • Global Accelerator improves speed but adds its own fee
Exam tip

Cutting the bill by cutting distance, hops and bytes beats buying more bandwidth.

CDN and Edge Caching Cost

Lever Effect
CloudFront Caches at the edge; fewer origin requests
AWS origin to CloudFront Data transfer is not charged
CloudFront egress Usually cheaper than egress from the Region
Price classes Use fewer edge Regions to lower price
Cache hit ratio Longer TTLs, versioned file names, compression
Edge functions Handle simple work without the origin
  • Origin Shield adds a caching layer to cut origin load
Exam tip

Global users downloading large files: CloudFront cuts both latency and egress cost.

3Edge, load balancing, throttling, review and practice

Load Balancing and DNS Cost

Item Cost point
Load balancers Hourly plus capacity units; consolidate and delete idle
Cross-zone balancing Always on for an ALB; off by default on an NLB, where inter-AZ data can be charged
Route 53 hosted zones A monthly fee per zone
Route 53 queries Charged per million; alias queries to AWS resources are free
Routing policies Latency, geolocation, failover add health checks
  • Use alias records to AWS resources instead of CNAMEs where possible
  • Health checks cost money: use only those you need
Exam tip

Alias to an ALB or CloudFront costs nothing in queries; prefer it.

Throttling and Bandwidth Allocation

Tool What it controls
API Gateway throttling and usage plans Requests per second and quotas per client
AWS WAF rate-based rules Block floods before they reach costly back ends
SQS buffering Smooth bursts so the back end can be smaller
Lambda reserved concurrency Caps how much a function can scale and cost
Direct Connect and VPN sizing Buy bandwidth that matches the measured need
  • One VPN vs several: add tunnels only when throughput demands it
  • Right-size a Direct Connect port; link aggregation can add capacity
Exam tip

Unexpected traffic spikes raising the bill: throttle at the edge, not with bigger servers.

Reviewing Existing Workloads

Tool What it reveals
Cost Explorer by usage type Data transfer and NAT line items
Cost and Usage Report + Athena Resource-level network cost
VPC Flow Logs Who talks to whom, and how much
Trusted Advisor Idle load balancers, unused Elastic IPs
Cost allocation tags Network cost by team or project
  • Look for cross-AZ and cross-Region traffic and S3 through NAT
  • Check public IPv4 addresses you do not need
  • Budgets alert on spend; consolidated billing pools usage across accounts
Exam tip

Find the line item first, then the route that creates it.

Choosing the Cheapest Network Design

  • Private servers to S3 or DynamoDB: gateway endpoint
  • Global downloads: CloudFront
  • Steady, large hybrid: Direct Connect; quick or small: VPN
  • Many VPCs: Transit Gateway; few: peering
  • Test internet access: one shared NAT gateway

Exam tip

Name the traffic path, then remove the costliest hop.

What the Exam Asks: Cost-Optimized Networks

  • Which NAT layout: shared, per AZ or regional
  • Which connection: Direct Connect, VPN or internet
  • Which VPC link: peering, Transit Gateway or PrivateLink
  • Which route avoids NAT, cross-AZ or cross-Region charges
  • Which edge or throttling control reduces cost
Exam tip

Look for the clues: test, steady, global, S3 through NAT, many VPCs, spikes.

Design Check: Lantern and Loom Trims the Network Bill

Requirement Design
Three NAT gateways in a test VPC One shared NAT gateway
S3 through NAT Gateway endpoint
Overseas shoppers downloading images CloudFront with S3 origin
Steady, large feed to head office Direct Connect
Four VPCs that must talk Transit Gateway, or peering if few
Traffic spikes Throttling, WAF rate limits
Find the waste Cost Explorer usage types, Flow Logs
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Private EC2 instances at Lantern and Loom read terabytes from S3 every day through a NAT gateway, and the NAT data processing charge is large. How can the architect reduce the cost?

  • AAdd a second NAT gateway in another Availability Zone
  • BMove the instances to a public subnet with Elastic IP addresses
  • CCreate an S3 gateway endpoint and route S3 traffic to it
  • DReplace the NAT gateway with a NAT instance
Show the answer

Answer: C. A gateway endpoint for S3 has no additional charge and keeps S3 traffic off the NAT gateway, so the per-GB processing charge disappears. A second gateway adds cost, public IPv4 addresses bill hourly, and a NAT instance still carries the traffic.

S2The Lantern and Loom test VPC has three subnets in three Availability Zones, each with its own NAT gateway. Test servers do not need high availability, and the team wants the lowest NAT cost. What should they do?

  • AUse one shared NAT gateway for all test subnets
  • BKeep one NAT gateway per Availability Zone in the test VPC
  • CReplace each NAT gateway with a Transit Gateway attachment
  • DAdd a Site-to-Site VPN connection beside each gateway
Show the answer

Answer: A. Non-production workloads can accept a single shared NAT gateway, which removes two hourly charges, at the cost of cross-zone traffic and a single zone as the failure point. One per zone is for production resilience, and a Transit Gateway or VPN does not replace NAT.

S3Which TWO statements about network cost are correct? (Select TWO.)

  • AData transfer into AWS from the internet is charged at the highest rate
  • BGateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB have no additional charge
  • CTraffic between instances in different Availability Zones is always free
  • DData transfer from an AWS origin to CloudFront is not charged
  • EDirect Connect has no port charge
Show the answer

Answer: B, D. Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB add no charge, and data moving from an AWS origin to CloudFront is not charged. Inbound internet traffic is free, cross-AZ traffic is charged, and Direct Connect bills port hours.

S4Lantern and Loom sends a large, steady data feed to its head office every day. Internet egress is costly, and the feed needs consistent latency. Which connection lowers the per-GB cost and gives steady performance?

  • AAn internet connection with a larger instance
  • BAn AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the internet
  • CA second VPC peering connection
  • DAWS Direct Connect
Show the answer

Answer: D. Direct Connect bills port hours plus a lower data-out rate and gives consistent latency, which suits steady, high-volume transfer. A VPN rides the internet, and VPC peering connects VPCs, not an office.

S5Overseas shoppers download large product images from an S3 bucket in one Region, and the data-out charges are high. What should the architect add to cut cost and latency?

  • AA NAT gateway placed in front of the bucket
  • BA CloudFront distribution with the bucket as origin
  • CA second bucket in the same Region as the first
  • DAn S3 gateway endpoint for the overseas shoppers
Show the answer

Answer: B. CloudFront caches images near viewers, serves them at a lower egress price than direct S3 transfer, and S3-to-CloudFront transfer is not charged. A NAT gateway or a gateway endpoint does not serve internet viewers, and a second bucket does not cut distance.

5Quick Reference Card

  • Data in is free; out, cross-Region and cross-AZ are charged
  • NAT: shared for test, per AZ for production; gateway endpoints avoid NAT charges
  • Connect: Direct Connect for steady, large; VPN for quick; peering for few, Transit Gateway for many
  • Reduce bytes: CloudFront, caching, compression, throttling
  • Review: Cost Explorer usage types, Flow Logs, Trusted Advisor
